title: A weakly initial object and small wide equalizers give an initial object
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$. Let $\mathcal C$ be an ordinary category [def-nagata-category] with $\mathcal U$-small Hom sets. Suppose it has all $\mathcal U$-small wide equalizers: for any objects $X,Y$ and any $\mathcal U$-small family $(f_i:X\to Y)_{i\in I}$, there are an object $E$ and arrows $e:E\to X$, $q:E\to Y$ with $f_i e=q$ for all $i$, universal among such pairs of arrows. This includes $I=\varnothing$, when the universal pair is a product of $X$ and $Y$. If an object $T\in\mathcal C$ is weakly initial, meaning $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(T,Z)\ne\varnothing$ for every object $Z$, then $\mathcal C$ has an initial object $0$: for every $Z$, there is exactly one arrow $0\to Z$.
